subject: Budgetary request: Storix prepay options and year-by-year split
participants_external: Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@storix.com> - Head of Infrastructure, Storix
messages:
From: Ava Bloor <ava.bloor@storix.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-07T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: FY27 ask: prepay options & high-level pro forma

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick intro earlier. Storix is starting FY27 budget planning and we need a concise budgetary quote for the platform ahead of our board review next month. High level details:

- Expected average monthly tokens: ~2.5B tokens (text generation & embeddings mixed)
- Expected ramp: 50% of that in Q1, 80% by Q3, full run-rate by Q4
- Interested in: 1) annual prepay (contracted for 1 year), 2) multi-year prepay (2–3 year) with term discounts, and 3) whether you offer ramp schedules or milestone credits for phased adoption

Can you send a pro forma invoice we can drop into procurement showing year-by-year invoice lines for (a) hosted API usage, (b) dedicated pool reserved capacity (if applicable), and (c) any private/on-prem add-ons? Also: please call out billing cadence, refund/true-up mechanics, and any early termination exposure.

We may need the doc by end of week — our procurement lead Marcus will be copied on follow-ups.

Thanks,
Ava
Ava Bloor
CFO, Storix
[Attachment: storix_budget_template.xlsx (requested)]

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Bloor <ava.bloor@storix.com>
Cc: Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@storix.com>
Date: 2026-06-07T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FY27 ask: prepay options & high-level pro forma

Ava —

Appreciate the clear brief. Attached is a budgetary pro forma and an illustrative ramp schedule that maps your stated token profile to line-item invoices. High level options included in the attachment:

1) Annual prepay (1 year) — baseline pricing with a 5% prepay discount vs pay-as-you-go; invoices issued up-front quarterly (option for annual up-front invoice)
2) Two-year prepay — 12% term discount applied to committed spend if billed as a single up-front prepayment or split over the first year (we can model both)
3) Three-year prepay — 18–20% term discount depending on minimum annual commitment and inclusion of support/observability add-ons

Ramp schedule suggestion (in attached XLS):
- Year 1: commit 60% of forecasted FY usage billed at signed-year rates, with milestones at quarter boundaries to release additional reserved capacity
- Year 2+: incremental usage billed at discounted committed rates; we can structure a true-up each quarter with credits applied to the next invoice

Key commercial notes:
- We do not do cash refunds for unused committed spend; instead we offer quarterly true-ups that credit future invoices for under-utilization or allow scope migration across Redwood products (hosted <-> dedicated) with prior notice
- Private/on-prem pricing is quoted separately and typically includes a one-time deployment/validation fee; I included a sample line item in the pro forma
- Taxes and wiring instructions are not shown on the budgetary doc — finance will append these on the formal invoice

Attachments: Storix_FY27_proforma_prepay_v1.pdf, Storix_prepay_ramp_schedule.xlsx

Next steps: please confirm (a) whether you want an annual up-front invoice vs quarterly billed prepay, and (b) target committed amount for Year 1 so I can produce a signature-ready pro forma for procurement. If helpful, I can join a 30-minute call with Marcus and your procurement/legal to walk the doc.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
[Attachment: Storix_FY27_proforma_prepay_v1.pdf]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, Ava Bloor <ava.bloor@storix.com>
Cc: Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@storix.com>, nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-07T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FY27 ask: prepay options & high-level pro forma

Looping in finance (Marissa here) for a few procurement specifics — quick notes to add to the formal pro forma:

- We can present either an annual up-front invoice or split the prepay across quarterly invoices for accounting friendliness. Annual up-front yields the largest term discount bands.
- Invoice lines will include tax gross-up and a separate bank/wire instruction PDF; please note our standard wire terms are NET 30 from invoice date unless a different arrangement is requested.
- For private/on-prem we include a capital equipment line (where applicable) and a separate services line for deployment & SOW work — those can be amortized per request but need to be explicit to procurement.
- If Storix requires a refund clause for unused prepay, we can offer a limited buy-back at a defined lower rate for the first 60 days post-activation, otherwise the standard is credit/true-up.

I've attached a concise commercial summary we typically provide to procurement: Redwood_TermSummary_v2.pdf

- Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_TermSummary_v2.pdf]

From: Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@storix.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-08T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FY27 ask: prepay options & high-level pro forma

Thanks Vanessa / Marissa — couple of procurement clarifications from my side: 

- Can you break out hosted API spend vs Dedicated Reserved pool vs Private deployment as separate top-level invoice lines with per-year burn estimates? Our procurement team needs explicit line items for our capital vs OPEX planning.
- For the multi-region usage we expect some traffic to land in EU regions — does the term discount change if we specify region-bound capacity? If so, please show a split.
- Refunds: we understand credits/true-ups are typical, but procurement will push for a limited pro-rated refund if our committed usage ends up < 50% after year 1. Is there a middle ground (e.g., prorated buy-back at 40% of effective rate)?

If you can provide an updated pro forma with those three breakout lines and a year-by-year invoice schedule, we can run it through procurement next Tuesday.

-Marcus
Marcus Liu
Head of Infrastructure, Storix
[marcus.liu@storix.com]

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Bloor <ava.bloor@storix.com>, Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@storix.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FY27 ask: prepay options & high-level pro forma

Marcus / Ava —

Thanks for the excellent clarifying questions. I updated the pro forma to include:

- Separate top-level lines: Hosted API (consumption), Dedicated Reserved Pool (monthly equivalent committed), Private/On-prem (one-time + annual support). Each line is shown per-year for 3 years in the attached PDF.
- Regional note: term discounts are consistent across regions; if you elect region-bound reserved capacity we will show a region surcharge line for EU capacity (approx +8% on dedicated unit rates) — included as an optional line item in Year 1.
- Refund/Buy-back: we can offer a limited prorated buy-back within the first 90 days at 40% of the effective committed rate (applies to committed dedicated spend only). Outside that window, standard quarterly true-up credits apply. I called this out in the doc under "Prepay protections".

Attachments: Storix_FY27_proforma_prepay_v1.pdf (updated with breakout), Storix_prepay_ramp_schedule.xlsx

Next steps:
1) Please confirm the Year 1 committed amount you want modeled (I used a conservative 60% of your stated FY forecast in the attached — changeable).
2) If procurement wants the annual up-front invoice, indicate whether they will accept NET 30 or request alternate payment terms so finance can reflect that on the invoice.
3) If you'd like, I can set a 30-minute legal/procurement call Wednesday 6/11 to walk the pro forma and capture any SOW items for private deployment.

Happy to jump on the call — thanks again.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
[Attachment: Storix_FY27_proforma_prepay_v1.pdf]
